title: Successive THIS_AND_FUTURE Splits on an Already-Split Series (Multi-Split Chains)

citations.verbatim_quote: The "RANGE" parameter is used to specify the effective range of recurrence instances from the instance specified by the "RECURRENCE-ID" property value.  The value for the range parameter can only be "THISANDFUTURE" to indicate a range defined by the given recurrence instance and all subsequent instances.  Subsequent instances are determined by their "RECURRENCE-ID" value and not their current scheduled start time.  Subsequent instances defined in separate components are not impacted by the given recurrence instance.

Assuming an unbounded recurring calendar component scheduled to occur on Mondays and Wednesdays, the "RANGE" parameter could not be used to reschedule only the future Monday instances to occur on Tuesday instead.  In such cases, the calendar application could simply truncate the unbounded recurring calendar component (i.e., with the "COUNT" or "UNTIL" rule parts), and create two new unbounded recurring calendar components for the future instances.

1.  The primary key for referencing a particular iCalendar component is the "UID" property value.  To reference an instance of a recurring component, the primary key is composed of the "UID" and the "RECURRENCE-ID" properties.

   2.  The secondary key for referencing a component is the "SEQUENCE" property value.  For components where the "UID" and "RECURRENCE-ID" property values are the same, the component with the highest numeric value for the "SEQUENCE" property obsoletes all other revisions of the component with lower values.

rationale: Under the component-splitting `STORE_POLICY` (R-L3-001), splitting a recurring series at `T1` produces two recurring components sharing the same `UID`: Segment 1 (`RECURRENCE-ID=None, DTSTART=T0, RRULE=...;UNTIL=T1-1s, SEQUENCE=s0`) and Segment 2 (`RECURRENCE-ID=T1, DTSTART=T1_new, RRULE=..., SEQUENCE=s1`). When a user subsequently performs another `THIS_AND_FUTURE` edit or delete at a later occurrence `T2 > T1` (generated by Segment 2), Segment 1 is already bounded by `UNTIL = T1 - 1s < T2` and therefore does not generate `T2`. Only Segment 2 matches `T2`. Consequently, the second `THIS_AND_FUTURE` operation at `T2` must leave Segment 1 (`[T0, T1)`) completely untouched, truncate Segment 2's `RRULE` to `UNTIL = T2 - 1s`, and (in the case of an edit) fork a third recurring component Segment 3 (`RECURRENCE-ID=T2, DTSTART=T2_new, RRULE=..., SEQUENCE=s1+1`). Conversely, if a subsequent `THIS_AND_FUTURE` operation targets `T_early` inside Segment 1 (`T0 <= T_early < T1`), it truncates Segment 1 before `T_early` and removes all superseded downstream segments (`RECURRENCE-ID >= T_early`, including Segment 2).
store_implication:
1. Forward multi-split (`T2 > T1`): When a `THIS_AND_FUTURE` edit or delete targets `T2` on a series already split at `T1 < T2`: (a) the prior segment `[T0, T1)` (whose `UNTIL < T2`) does not match `T2` and MUST remain unchanged; (b) if `T2 > Segment2.dtstart`, Segment 2 MUST have its `RRULE` truncated to `UNTIL = T2 - delta` (and `COUNT` cleared or adjusted per R-L3-004 if forked), and for an `edit`, a new Segment 3 recurring component MUST be inserted with `uid = UID`, `recurrence_id = T2`, `sequence = Segment2.sequence + 1`, and the future `rrule`; (c) if `T2 == Segment2.dtstart` (targeting the very first occurrence of Segment 2), a `THIS_AND_FUTURE` delete removes Segment 2 altogether (leaving Segment 1 intact), and a `THIS_AND_FUTURE` edit updates Segment 2 in place (leaving Segment 1 intact).
2. Earlier re-split (`T_early < T1`): When a `THIS_AND_FUTURE` edit or delete targets `T_early` in Segment 1 (`T0 <= T_early < T1`), Segment 1 is truncated at `T_early` (or removed/replaced if `T_early == T0`) and any downstream split segments or overrides with `RECURRENCE-ID >= T_early` MUST be removed so superseded future segments do not remain active.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: 3-way split chain: A 6-day daily series (May 1..6) is first split at May 3 (`THIS_AND_FUTURE`, summary='Phase 2'), and then split again at May 5 (`THIS_AND_FUTURE`, summary='Phase 3'). The calendar must contain 3 recurring components: May 1..2 ('Phase 1', `UNTIL=20250503T085959`, `sequence=0`), May 3..4 ('Phase 2', `RECURRENCE-ID=20250503T090000`, `UNTIL=20250505T085959`, `sequence=1`), and May 5..6 ('Phase 3', `RECURRENCE-ID=20250505T090000`, `COUNT=2`, `sequence=2`).

Deleting THIS_AND_FUTURE at the exact start of Segment 2 (`T2 == T1`): must remove Segment 2 completely without deleting Segment 1 (unlike `T2 == T0` on an unsplit series, which deletes the entire series).

Deleting or splitting THIS_AND_FUTURE at `T_early` (e.g. May 2) after a prior split at `T1` (May 4): truncating only Segment 1 (`May 1..3`) while leaving Segment 2 (`May 4..6`) in the calendar would erroneously leave May 4..6 on the timeline after the user deleted or replaced 'May 2 and all future occurrences'.

scenarios.name: second_this_and_future_split_creates_three_segment_chain
scenarios.description: Applying a second THIS_AND_FUTURE edit on May 5 to a daily series (May 1..6) that was already split on May 3 leaves the May 1..2 segment untouched, truncates the May 3..6 segment with UNTIL=20250505T085959, and forks a third segment starting on May 5 with COUNT=2 and sequence=2.
